children: Stocks staged a rebound Friday morning, capping another roller-coaster week for U.S. markets.
The Nasdaq composite was trading 1% higher shortly after the open, while the S&P 500 and the Dow industrials rose 0.8% apiece.

It has been a choppy week in markets: After an epic rally on news of Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia, jitters around AI crept back in, knocking stocks lower. Investors now seem to be setting those concerns aside.

"There are so many signs of exhaustion of selling," said Gerry Fowler, an equity strategist at UBS. "You don't need anyone to choose to buy the market for it to go up. At these levels, you only need volatility to be slightly lower, and risk-control funds start to buy."

Trading is thin around the Thanksgiving break, Fowler said, meaning even a limited uptick in stock buying can translate into healthy-looking gains. U.S. markets were closed Thursday and will close early Friday.

All three major indexes are set to notch big weekly gains. Still, they are far off their recent highs: The S&P 500 and Dow are each more than 6% below their early October peaks while the Nasdaq, down more than 14% over the same period, is still in a correction.
The AI trade isn't out of the woods yet, XTB research director Kathleen Brooks said.

"The fundamental problems surrounding the AI trade remain," Brooks said. "The questions that caused the market panic are still unanswered, for example, concerns about the profitability of the AI trade and financing costs."

Friday's gains followed a bullish session in Asia. South Korea's tech-dominated Kospi index jumped 4.3%, while stocks in Shanghai and Hong Kong rose after Chinese authorities reiterated their support for capital markets. The tech-heavy ChiNext Price rose 11%, marking its best day in over two years.
European stocks also climbed, with AI-related stocks leading the charge.

Investors' renewed appetite for risk also sparked a rally in precious metals, which had tracked the recent AI selloff to hit their lowest levels of the year. Silver contracts jumped more than 10%, while gold futures gained close to 4% to trade around $3,665 a troy ounce.

U.S. Treasurys weakened amid hardened expectations for Federal Reserve rate increases in the coming months. Benchmark 10-year yields rose to trade above 4.9%. Yields rise when bond prices fall. The Fed enters a blackout period on Saturday ahead of its December meeting, where a quarter-point rise is broadly seen as a given, according to CME FedWatch.
An uptick in oil prices over the past few days could strengthen the case for rate increases. Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, were little changed at about $91.50 a barrel.
